subject: Shiny Server not sourcing server.R until web page is accessed?

messages.author: f0a3bc559c29cde3
messages.subject: Shiny Server not sourcing server.R until web page is accessed?
parts:
Hi all,

I am currently using shiny server to host an app.  This app requires a lot of data to be loaded and preprocessed (30-45 minutes).  It is also restarted every morning via a cron job.  This restart allows the server to read in and process the data from the previous day.  It appears that the call or start shiny-server (or restart shiny-server) will only load the ui.R page.  After waiting about an hour (more than enough time for server.R to finish running) I attempt to access the web page.  This page doesn't appear to have loaded any of the data, as it takes another 40 minutes or so before the data populates the screen.  Is there a way, possibly in a config or something, to force server.R to be sourced on a call to start shiny-server (or restart shiny-server) as opposed to waiting until the web page is being accessed?

I am new to setting up the server side of things, so if my issue isn't clear, I am more than happy to provide more detail.

Thanks a lot for all your help.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Shiny Server not sourcing server.R until web page is accessed?
parts:
An app that has 30-45 minute startup time is far outside the bounds of what we designed Shiny Server for. Have you considered doing the loading and preprocessing in a separate R process (managed by cron) outside of the Shiny app, and having it save its results in an .Rds file? Then the Shiny app can just refer to that .Rds file and load very quickly. This is a good general principle for Shiny: since doing computation in a Shiny app means a user is sitting there waiting, you want to preprocess/precompute/aggregate/summarize as much as you can offline.

You can even use reactiveFileReader so that even while the Shiny app is running, when the .Rds file is updated by the cron job, the data updates reactively--no need to restart the app.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Shiny Server not sourcing server.R until web page is accessed?
parts:
Being outside of the shinyServer(function) call but still in server.R means that it will be done once each time the Shiny app starts, which is different than when Shiny Server starts. The Shiny Server process is intended to be long-lived; it starts and stops Shiny apps (each of which runs in a different process, or even multiple processes in the case of Shiny Server Pro) as users come and go.

By default, Shiny Server is configured to assume that Shiny apps are relatively cheap to start and stop; it starts apps on demand and stops them just a few seconds after the last visitor to that app leaves.
